title: A Multiplexed System for Quantitative Comparisons of Chromatin Landscapes
boundary: T7-promoter/sample-index adapters are ligated to fragmented nucleosomes before immunoprecipitation. Indexed chromatin is pooled then split among ChIP assays; selected DNA undergoes IVT, reverse transcription and assay-index PCR. Pre-IP pool/split indexing plus RNA-mediated linear amplification is a distinct physical preparation from ChIPmentation or target-barcoded pA-Tn5 CoBATCH; MINUTE-ChIP is treated as a same-family successor, not another lead.

No final/AM recipe equivalence, SI, modified-oligo, linked-source or correction audit; no source-bundle acquisition. Exact DOI/name absent ours, expansion plan and round ledgers at discovery.

title: RSC-Associated Subnucleosomes Define MNase-Sensitive Promoters in Yeast
boundary: Antibody-targeted nuclease cleavage and release supplies chromatin complexes for a subsequent histone immunoprecipitation before sequencing. This serial release-then-selection boundary preserves a joint protein/histone population; it is not another CUT&RUN target or a downstream comparison of separate ChIP datasets. Later mammalian BAF application is not proposed separately.

title: ChIP-DIP maps binding of hundreds of proteins to DNA simultaneously and identifies diverse gene regulatory elements
boundary: Antibody-bead-oligonucleotide conjugates are pooled for ChIP; retained chromatin/bead assemblies undergo split-pool ligation so genomic DNA and antibody identifiers receive shared barcodes. Sequencing associates DNA with the selected antibody through a jointly barcoded physical complex. This differs from SPRITE spatial-contact clustering and target-coded Tn5 insertion; the antibody count alone is not the proposed distinction.
